claims.statement: Screening is an alternative project mode selected by Project.screening (ScreeningConfig | null); isScreening(project) returns true iff project.screening is set, and this single predicate is what every caller uses to branch into screening behavior.

A screening project's schema is never read from the file: loadProject derives it fresh from config.screening.reasons on every load via screeningSchemaDefs, and serializeProject writes the derived schema back so the file stays self-describing for non-SaiLoR readers while the on-disk reason list can never disagree with the dropdown the reviewer sees.

The derived schema is a fixed two-node shape: Decision is a two-option string enum (Include/Exclude) rather than a boolean, because the codebase's isEmptyValue/isUnanswered/hasAnnotations machinery treats a boolean as empty until true, which would make an Exclude checkbox unable to distinguish 'include' from 'not yet looked at'; Reason's options are a copy of config.screening.reasons.

ScreeningConfig is { reasons: string[] } and is the only authorable part of a screening schema; parseScreening trims, dedupes, drops blanks, and throws ProjectLoadError if no reasons survive, and the zod superRefine lets a screening project omit config.schema entirely while requiring it for everyone else.
DEFAULT_SCREENING_REASONS seeds a new screening project with ordinary SLR exclusion reasons including 'Other' as an authored escape hatch for a closed enum.

screeningStatus reads a tree as 'included'/'excluded'/'undecided', with any null/missing tree, missing node, or unrecognized value reading as 'undecided' (the conservative direction), so importFromScreening never silently drops a paper it merely cannot parse; screeningReason returns the reason only when meaningful and callers must check the status first.

screeningCounts returns PRISMA-style totals (total/included/excluded/undecided), a byReason map keyed by every configured reason including unused ones (PRISMA reports the pre-registered list in full), and an excludedWithoutReason bucket for excluded papers whose reason is blank or not configured; byReason is built with Object.create(null) so a hand-edited reason of 'constructor'/'__proto__' cannot collide with Object.prototype.

counts.ts is deliberately store-free: it imports the shared seatTree (src/model/seatTree.ts), which the store's currentTree also builds on (single-reviewer and Consolidation read paper.annotations; a numbered reviewer reads paper.reviews[n]; null reads nothing), so the module stays independently testable, never creates a reviewer's tree, and cannot drift from the store's routing.

pendingUnanimous counts papers holding any unanimous fill Consolidation has not adopted (decision, reason, or both) and drives the ScreeningPanel 'Adopt all' notice, while pendingUnanimousDecisions counts only still-undecided papers whose reviewers all chose the same decision and drives the screening-import dialog's 'not yet screened' count; the two are separate because the panel's button adopts everything but the dialog's promise is specifically about changing inclusion counts.
Both pending-unanimous counts delegate to unanimousFills (consolidate/unanimous.ts), the same agreement routine annotation consolidation uses, and are zero for a single-reviewer project.

reasonUsage.ts guards reason renames and deletes: countPapersUsingReason reports how many papers record a reason across both the consolidated annotations tree and each reviewer's tree (kept under extra.reviews in the editor's representation), and renameReasonInPapers rewrites from->to immutably preserving identity for unchanged papers and trees so dirty-tracking only marks what actually changed and === means no-op.

screeningIssues enforces the two cross-field rules the schema cannot express: Exclude requires a reason and Include must not have one; it issues kind:'screening' ValidationIssues, uses the same seatTree routing, reports malformed trees as no issues rather than throwing, and sets canonicalPath:'' so ValidationDialog falls back to a paper-only jump.

The store's validate action appends screeningIssues to ordinary schema validation issues over the original project (not the remapped papers) because screeningIssues reads decision and reason together rather than a single active tree.

App.tsx swaps the workspace panes based on project.screening: when set, the middle pane is ScreeningRecord (unless screeningShowPdf is on, then PdfViewer) and the right pane is ScreeningPanel instead of AnnotationPanel.

ScreeningRecord is the default middle-pane surface shown instead of PdfViewer because screening is normally a title+abstract decision and the PDF is often absent; it shows title/authors/venue/DOI/abstract, flags abstractFromPdf extractions as possibly incomplete, and exposes an untouched PdfViewer via a 'Read the PDF' button that flips screeningShowPdf.

ScreeningPanel is the right-pane decision control replacing AnnotationPanel: two buttons (Include via I, Exclude via E; pressing the active one clears it), a Reason ComboBox disabled unless excluded, a Summary button (plus Consolidation-only Agreement and Disagreements buttons), a Consolidation-only pending-unanimous notice with Adopt all, and a progress line; it withholds the form when no reviewer is picked in a multi-reviewer project.

setScreeningDecision writes both Decision and Reason in one mutation (clears the reason on any non-Exclude, writes a supplied reason when excluding via the 1-9 shortcuts so the exclusion and reason are one undo step), is refused in read-only mode and when a multi-reviewer project has no seat picked, reads wasUndecided before mutating, and auto-advances selection to the next undecided paper after the current one (stopping at the end rather than wrapping) when transitioning from undecided to a non-null decision; setScreeningReason is a no-op unless the seat's own decision is Exclude, delegating to setFieldValue otherwise.

adoptAllUnanimousScreening iterates every paper calling adoptUnanimousValues with coalescing so the batch is one undo step, returns the filled-paper count, and is synchronous because screening has no repeatable node (unlike the annotation path's adoptAllUnanimousAnnotations).

ScreeningSummary is a PRISMA-counts modal (ValidationDialog pattern, Escape/backdrop close) showing total/included/excluded/undecided plus a per-reason table for every configured reason and an excludedWithoutReason row when non-zero, labeled by which seat it counts.

ScreeningImportDialog is a pre-commit summary shown before writing: included papers are always carried, excluded never carried (with per-reason breakdown), undecided carried by default with an explicit 'leave them out' escape hatch; for target:'start' a radio chooses annotation vs second-screening project; when reviewers>1 and pendingUnanimousCount>0 it advises opening as Consolidation and using Adopt all first.

ScreeningReasonsEditor replaces SchemaTreeEditor for screening drafts and manages the ordered exclusion-reason list (order drives the 1-9 key shortcuts); on a committed rename it offers via confirm to migrate papers recording the old label (migrateScreeningReason), and on a remove it warns the same way since there is no new label to migrate to.

Screening keybindings are bare letters/numbers only, never while typing in a field or while any modal is open (a DOM check for .modal-overlay covers every dialog so a keypress inside a dialog cannot act on the hidden paper): I/E/U set Include/Exclude/undecided and 1-9 exclude with the Nth configured reason.

A screening project uses the same split storage as annotation but with a different prefix: reviewer files are screening-<n>.json (not reviewer-<n>.json) and the consolidated file is screening-consolidated.json (not consolidated.json); splitProjectFiles and ownAnnotationPathMatcher derive the prefix from project.screening, which lets a screening-to-full-text sibling relationship keep working without file collisions.

startFromScreening and importFromScreening pick/parse a screening project (refusing one whose screening is null), partition it into included (always carried)/undecided (carried by default)/excluded (never carried, with per-reason tally) by reading each paper's consolidated annotations tree (the result that ships), set a screeningImport draft, and resolveScreeningImport commits the carried papers into a new sibling project (named -fulltext or -annotation) or the open session.

importFromScreening is blocked when the open project is itself a screening project; a carried row arrives undecided under the open project's own reasons, but in-place import into screening stays blocked because the two-pass workflow is fully served by startFromScreening.

An imported project records a ProjectProvenance with kind:'screening-import', the source file name (never its absolute path, since files are committed to git and shared), the import time, and a counts snapshot (included/undecided/excluded/carried) that is not derivable later because screening continues in the source after import; carried is the number PRISMA's flow diagram wants.

partitionScreeningPapers and its excludedByReason tally use Object.create(null) so a hand-edited reason of 'constructor'/'__proto__' cannot collide with Object.prototype and drop a row from the import dialog.

The ScreeningImportDraft distinguishes target:'start' (fresh editor session, where startKind chooses annotation vs screening) from target:'import' (add rows into the already-open session, whose kind is already fixed), carries the source's own ScreeningConfig to seed a second-screening target's reason list, and stores pendingUnanimousCount (decisions only) plus the source's reviewer count and every source id to avoid annotations-folder collisions.

The project editor's screening checkbox (setScreening) turns screening on by seeding DEFAULT_SCREENING_REASONS or off by setting screening to null, as its own undo step; on save the screening target's reason list is seeded from the source screening project's own reasons rather than the generic defaults, and its reviewer count is inherited for a second screening pass but not for the annotation target.

screeningMarksByPaper collects a screening project's PDF highlights for the importing project's papers: each paper is matched to its screening counterpart by id, then by the id with a numeric suffix stripped (p1 -> p1-2), then by the same certain duplicate match the import itself uses (DOI, or title with authors and year), and the matched paper's consolidated marks plus each reviewer's reviewMarks in seat order are tagged with their seat; papers with no counterpart or no marks are left out.

loadScreeningMarks runs after openProject/openRecent (never after resyncProjectFromDisk), only for a project with provenance kind 'screening-import' that is not itself a screening project and has a saved path; it asks the platform for the screening source sibling, parses it, and stores screeningMarksByPaper keyed by the importing project's paper ids, treating an unreadable or missing source as simply no marks; screeningMarks is cleared by closeProject and loadFromText.

The Rust screeningSource command treats the provenance's source file name as untrusted input: it reads the sibling only when it is a plain .json file name (no path separators, not a dotfile, not the project's own file, not a symlink) and only for a project opened this session, so a crafted provenance field cannot become an arbitrary file-system read.

A screening project's annotation project consumes the carried highlights read-only: AnnotationPanel shows a 'Show markings from screening (N)' checkbox only for papers the screening marked, and PdfViewer renders the ticked marks as a non-interactive overlay (no popover; dragging across one still selects text), labelled with screeningSeatLabel as 'Screening, consolidated' or 'Screening, Reviewer N'.

Screening's PDF-highlight files use their own name family too: screening-marks-<n>.json and screening-marks-consolidated.json rather than marks-*.json. marksFileName and parseMarksFileName derive and recognize the name from the screening flag, with a screening project's pre-rename marks-*.json read as legacy; both read paths (the assembler in assemble.ts, wrapped by assembleProject in tauri.ts, and projectFromFiles) process legacy files first so a file under the kind's own name wins, and the assembler drops a legacy marks file when an annotation sibling sharing the folder lists the same paper id.

For a screening project, the paper list replaces the five-state completeness dot with a tri-state status marker (status-dot screening-<status>, from paperScreeningStatus over currentTree routing) with readiness relegated to its tooltip, replaces the annotation-state filter dropdown with a four-button segmented control writing screeningFilter ('all'/'undecided'/'included'/'excluded'), and its progress line reads 'N of M screened'; completenessApplies is false for a screening project, which is the one rule that removes the finished checkbox, the completeness fill, and the annotation-state filter together.

For a screening project, agreementInput restricts the inter-rater statistic to the Decision field only (the exclusion reason is a different question, one defined only on papers both reviewers excluded, and is filtered out entirely rather than counted as 'skipped'), and ConsolidationDialog hides the 'these mean the same thing' equality checkbox for the Decision field so a consolidator cannot declare Include and Exclude equivalent.

extractScreeningAbstract fires on paper selection (selectPaper) and for the project's landing paper in loadFromText, never on the screeningShowPdf toggle; it reads the PDF with the same source the viewer renders, marks what it writes abstractFromPdf, skips papers that already have an abstract, and tracks per-paper session state (screeningAbstractReads: 'reading' in flight, 'none' once a read found nothing) so a PDF with no recognisable abstract is not re-fetched on every reselect while a successful read leaves no entry (the abstract itself is the guard, so undoing it lets extraction run again). Staleness is keyed on projectGeneration (bumped only when the project is replaced or closed), and the write deliberately pushes no undo entry.

Screening keybindings are bare letters/numbers only, never while typing in a field or while a modal, error overlay, or open dropdown menu is on screen (a DOM check for '.modal-overlay, .error-overlay, .menu' covers every dialog, so a keypress inside a dialog cannot act on the hidden paper): I/E/U set Include/Exclude/undecided and 1-9 exclude with the Nth configured reason, with a digit past the end of the list left to the browser.

ScreeningPanel's Include and Exclude buttons and the Reason ComboBox carry the AI-fill mark via useAiMark (the same light-blue ai-marked border annotation fields get, cleared when the reviewer interacts), so an applied AI screening proposal stays visibly the app's doing until looked at.
